description: Three independent cleanups, none of which touches the construction pipeline that is praxis's uncontested differentiator. **(1) `praxis/s3.py` + `tests/mocks3.py` (508) hand-roll an AWS SigV4 signing chain and an XML `ListObjectsV2` scanner** for list/get/put/delete — four operations `minio-py` covers 1:1. **(2) 896 lines of DEAD legacy generators** (`generate_notebooks.py` 691 + `enhance_notebooks.py` 205, **6.6% of the repo**), superseded by `praxis/construct.py` and unreachable — `enhance_notebooks.py` is a `str.format()` engine over a literal `.ipynb` JSON string template with `{{`/`}}` escaping. **(3) `nbformat` is a DECLARED HARD DEPENDENCY that no production writer imports** — `construct.py:269-303` and `scaffold_notebooks.py:131-136` hand-build cell dicts instead. That is the bridge-is-not-an-adoption pattern, and fixing it also unblocks D10's nbgrader metadata work, since nbgrader reads and writes through nbformat.

userStories.title: Use the nbformat that is already a dependency
userStories.description: Hand-built cell dicts become library calls — the swap that also unblocks nbgrader.
acceptanceCriteria: Produced notebooks are byte-compared against the current output where the format allows, and any difference is explained rather than accepted silently.
The path is now open for nbgrader's cell metadata (D10) without a second notebook writer.
`nbformat` moves from declared-and-unused to declared-and-used — assert it is imported by the production writer.
userStories.notes: Smallest change here, largest downstream unlock. Do it first.

userStories.title: Replace the hand-rolled S3 client and delete the dead generators
acceptanceCriteria: `praxis/s3.py` is replaced by **minio-py** (1,071★ Apache-2.0) — `Minio(...).{list_objects,get_object,put_object,remove_object}` covers the whole surface; `tests/mocks3.py` retires in favour of the vendor's test double or moto. **obstore** (794★ MIT) is the alternative if a Rust-backed client is preferred; state the choice.
`generate_notebooks.py` and `enhance_notebooks.py` are DELETED after confirming zero reachability from `construct.py` or any CLI entry point.
The stdlib-only posture is corrected in the docs: it was costing 508 lines including a signing chain, in an app that already ships FastAPI/uvicorn/jupyterlab in its `launch` extra.
The removed line count is reported.
userStories.notes: 896 dead lines is 6.6% of the repo. Confirm unreachability, then delete rather than deprecating.

userStories.title: Give the LLM transport real retry semantics
userStories.description: This is a correctness bug, not a preference.
acceptanceCriteria: `praxis/llm.py`'s `_urlopen` moves to **httpx** and `complete()` is wrapped in **tenacity** with exponential backoff and jitter, retrying on 429 and 5xx.

Today `DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS = 3` with **no sleep, no backoff, no jitter**, and an `LLMError` consumes an attempt immediately — assert the new behaviour actually waits and actually distinguishes retryable failures.
The 4-way provider router and the `AGORA_BASE_URL` hook are PRESERVED — those are the product; only the transport changes.
userStories.notes: A 429 currently burns all three attempts in milliseconds and fails the construction run.
